title: There's no place like home: Ian Conerly-Goodly returns to Southeastern for senior season - NewsBreak
text: HAMMOND, La. — The last time we saw Ian Conerly-Goodly rep the green and gold at Strawberry Stadium was the 2023 season, when the First-Team All-Conference selection led the Lions with 109 tackles. “I feel like my sophomore year, yes, it was a good season, but that wasn’t the best football I could put on tape. Just being wiser and older, I just know the game more, and I’ll be able to play faster,” said Southeastern senior Ian Conerly-Goodly. Ian Conerly-Goodley transferred to Troy in 2024, where his football growth accelerated in just one year with the Trojans. “I learned how to fight through adversity, especially playing through an injury. I hurt myself on a Tuesday practice before the first game against Nevada. Just coming back and playing a whole season on an injury, I learned that I could fight through anything, and I was just blessed to be able to stay healthy and produce like I did,” said Coneryl-Goodly. Ian Conerly-Goodly excelled at Troy, recording 54 tackles and a pick-six in their regular season finale. A month and a half later, the Covington native decided the best place to close out his college career was 30 minutes down I-12 in the place where it all started. “It’s just home in Hammond. I love the people here, the camaraderie on the team, the people on the staff. It’s just all love here, and I love the culture that we have, the standard. We’re a hard-nosed football team that is going to come and play our hardest every time we step on the field,” added Conerly-Goodly. That hunger and determination are shared by Ian Conerly-Goodly and a Southeastern roster that returns 16 starters from a team that was three points away from a Southland title shot in 2024. “We have the most depth that I’ve had since being here as a freshman. Like, this team excites me because we have depth at every level, especially on defense. We have veterans at every level, all conference players at every level. And just the communication, we’ve taken it to the next level. And it’s like we’re just playing for our brothers,” said Conerly-Goodly. Southeastern opens the regular season against Louisiana Tech on Saturday, August 30th. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to WGNO.
